headline: Coral trafficking ring exposed on Aegean island: What is red coral used for and how big is the threat?
body of the article: Greek authorities have arrested members of an Italian coral smuggling ring apprehended on the Aegean island of Skopelos. The Italian nationals are believed to have removed red coral from theseabedat an estimated value of around €800,000, with the cargo destined for Italy. The case is under investigation, and officials are also examining the exact route the coral would have followed after leavingGreece. The recent operation by Greece's General Directorate of Financial Transactions Control Forces (DEOS) is just a small piece of a much larger story. Red coral has been harvested for centuries in different parts of theMediterraneanand is the subject of an international trade in which Italy has historically played a central role. The town of Torre del Greco, near Naples, has become Europe's main centre for coral processing and jewellery making. Coral from different areas of the Mediterranean is channelled to the Italian market, where the raw material is turned into jewellery and other, higher value products. This activity is legal when the coral has been collected in line with the rules in force in each country. The problem begins when the raw material comes from illegal harvesting and then enters the same commercial chain. Related Most of the Maldives may be unliveable in 50 years – but these kayaking islanders aren't giving up Western Europe sets new temperature record hitting 900 million people worldwide The value of red coral varies greatly, depending on its quality, size and stage of processing. A report by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) on the future of precious red coral in the Mediterranean notes that top-quality coral can fetch up to €5,000 per kilo. Demand has risen in recent years, as redcoralhas made a comeback in the collections of major international fashion houses. Its presence in contemporary collections of luxury jewellery, clothing and accessories, including from houses such as Van Cleef & Arpels and Dolce & Gabbana, has put a material with a long history back at the centre of the luxury market. This development is particularly significant for a raw material that is by nature limited: red coral grows extremely slowly and large colonies take decades to form. Its high value has spawned a parallel, illegal market, with smuggling routes from countries in southern Europe and North Africa into Europe. In Algeria, according to research by the Earth Journalism Network, up to three tonnes of coral are believed to be trafficked illegally to Europe every year, with Italy among the key destinations. Bracelets made with turquoise, 925 silver, carnelian, red coral and green aventurine, archive image - AP Photo One of the biggest problems is traceability. Once raw coral reaches processing workshops and is turned into jewellery, it becomes far more difficult to determine where it came from. Related Arctic seabed mission documents fragile marine life threatened by Norway's deep-sea mining plans This is one of the reasons why the General Fisheries Commission for the Mediterranean (GFCM) of the UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) has carried out a dedicated research programme on red coral. Seven Mediterranean countries took part in the programme, which ran from 2020 to 2023, including Greece through the Hellenic Centre for Marine Research (HCMR). The aim was to improve knowledge of the status of coral populations and to strengthen management and traceability mechanisms. In Greece, however, significant gaps in knowledge remain. "Theseabeds of Greecehave not been mapped", explains Maria Salomidi, HCMR researcher and lead investigator. Researchers have identified areas with coral formations, but they do not yet have a full picture of the extent of the populations. At the same time, the seabed is under pressure from different activities. As Salomidi points out, both professional and recreational fishing can affectcoral ecosystems, even when the coral itself is not the target. The GFCM has warned that red coral populations may be in a state of overexploitation. And the Skopelos case, according to Salomidi, is unlikely to be an isolated incident: "The only thing I could safely say is that if one incident has been detected, many more have certainly occurred." Red coral (Corallium rubrum) is not a plant but a marine animal that forms colonies in the deep sea. With a hard calcareous skeleton, it grows extremely slowly, and a large, mature colony can take up to 100 years to form. Humanity's relationship with coral long predates the modern jewellery market. Traces of it have been found at prehistoric archaeological sites, and since antiquity it has been prized for its beauty and rarity and credited with protective and healing properties. Red coral colonies found at depths of more than 70 m in Greece by the HCMR/FAO survey - ΕΛΚΕΘΕ/FAO Its story is even intertwined with one of the Mediterranean's best-known myths. In Ovid'sMetamorphoses, Perseus, returning after beheading Medusa, stops to rest and lays her head on the seaweed. The Gorgon's blood drips onto it and, according to the myth, the soft plants turn to stone and take on a crimson colour. This, the ancient tale says, is how coral was born. Almost 2,000 years later, the myth still features in international scientific presentations on red coral. Its real story, however, has become far more complex: an organism that needs decades to grow has been turned into a valuable raw material for an international market, while scientists are still trying to record how much of this natural wealth remains in the Mediterranean.

headline: 7.4 earthquake strikes western Colombia, killing at least 111 people
body of the article: A strong earthquake with a magnitude of 7.4 struck western Colombia on Monday, killing at least 111 people, injuring at least 87 and causing major damage across the region. It was the largest quake to hit the South American country on record. The epicenter was in San José del Palmar, a community in the rural Chocó province about 250 miles west of Colombia's capital, Bogotá, the U.S. Geological Survey and its counterpart in Colombia reported. The quake hit at about 8:34 a.m. ET and was followed by a 5.0 magnitude aftershock less than an hour later, USGS reported. "You are not alone," Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella said in a video message. "Colombia has a president who cares about the people and who will do everything in his power to help them in the most difficult moments." Most of the deaths were reported in provinces neighboring Chocó, including at least 40 in the Risaralda region, where the hard-hit city of Pereira is located, and 27 in the Valle del Cauca region, where Colombia's third-biggest city, Cali, is located. Chocó Gov. Nubia Carolina Córdoba-Curisaid on social mediathat at least 12 people had died in her province. Four deathswere reportedin the city of Manizales in the Caldas region. A 73-year-old man died in the Antioquia province, thegovernor said. The earthquake prompted evacuations as far away as Bogotá. Witnesses reported feeling the shaking across the capital and all the way to the coast in Barranquilla, as well as in Ecuador to the south. About 10.5 million people experienced strong to very strong shaking, according to USGS. "The quake was very, very strong," Valeria Polo, a 29-year-old content creator in Bogotá, told the Agence France-Presse news agency. The quake left cities, including Cali, Manizales, Pereira and Quibdó, ravaged with a mix of residents and search teams picking through the rubble of collapsed buildings. More than 20 municipalities across the country had been hit and hundreds of buildings were damaged, officials said. In Cali, a city of 2 million people, there were 30 collapsed structures,Mayor Alejandro Eder saidon social media. Eder urged residents to remain calm and report any damage as soon as possible. Jorge Moncayo, a 64-year-old taxi driver in Cali, said he saw plumes of dust shoot up across the city from his home. "My entire house shook," he said. "I've never lived through such a powerful earthquake." Pereira's mayor, Mauricio Salazar, told a local radio station that at least 18 people had died in the city and that many more were trapped under "a massive quantity of collapsed buildings." At the airport in Pereira,videosshowed pieces of the ceiling falling down on travelers taking shelter and screaming, and people running through rubble in a panic. ManizalesMayor Jorge Eduardo Rojas saidon social media that 17 buildings in the city had collapsed and 19 had partially collapsed. Images showed one of the towers of the city's neo-Gothic cathedral hadcollapsedand fallen on the nave. Flights were suspended at multiple airports, including in Pereira, Manizales, Armenia, Cartago and Buenaventura, Colombia's aviation agency said. In Armenia, several people have been evacuated from their homes over structural damage fears. No structural damage was reported in Bogotá,Mayor Carlos F. Galán said. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in asocial media poston Monday that the Trump administration was closely monitoring the earthquake and "stands ready to support the people of Colombia." South Florida organizations are among U.S.-based humanitarian groups mobilizing to send aid to Colombia. "There's a lot of damage, and we are waiting for information as to what the needs are. The first is rescue and recovery," Fabio Andrade, the city of Weston's commissioner and a Colombian American, toldCBS Miami. Monday's earthquake was the strongest to hit Colombia since record-keeping started in the early 1920s. The country lies along the "Ring of Fire," the line of seismic faults encircling the Pacific Ocean where most of the world's earthquakes occur. The area where the quake struck, Colombia's coffee region, was devastated by anearthquake in 1999that killed more than 1,200 people. The seismic activity in Colombia also follows two back-to-back 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude quakes thatstruck neighboring Venezuelain late June, which causedwidespread damageand killed more than 5,000 people.

headline: Huge fire breaks out at Libya’s Zawiya refinery after drone attack
body of the article: Firefighters in Libya are battling a massive blaze at the Zawiya refinery following a drone attack, with the country's national oil company warning it may declare a force majeure and shut down operations if attacks continue. Libya's Ambulance and Emergency Service said in a statement on Tuesday there were no "serious injuries" from the fire, with most patients treated for smoke inhalation. Footage verified by Al Jazeera showed huge flames and thick black ‌smoke billowing over the facility, the largest operating refinery in Libya with a refining capacity of 120,000 barrels per day. It is located about 40km (25 miles) west of the capital, Tripoli. The National Oil Corporation (NOC) said in a statement on Facebook that the fire broke out on Monday evening at tank number 402-T, belonging to the Brega Oil Company. It said the tank, which contained about 4.5 million litres (1.2 million gallons) of gasoline, was "directly targeted, resulting in a severe fire before the tank completely collapsed". The NOC said the attack followed drone strikes on a water desalination plant at the refinery on Sunday and on a naphtha reservoir on Saturday. The company declared a "maximum emergency" in the region and urged authorities to launch an investigation and bring the perpetrators to justice. There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the attacks, and the company did ‌not say who they believed was behind them. In a statement hours later, the NOC said the refinery was "still being subject to sabotage attacks" with a drone targeting an oil blending and filling ⁠plant operated by the Zawiya Oil Refining Company. It said the drone fell near its main oil tank and a pipeline network used to produce oils for the domestic market, without causing any casualties or damage. "The company's board of directors also confirms that if these attacks continue, it will have to declare a state of force majeure and suspend operations at the refinery," it warned. The Brega Oil Company, meanwhile, appealed to "all parties to stop the fighting and stay away from oil facilities and depots". It said "oil facilities are vital infrastructure and owned by all Libyans" and that "protecting them is a national responsibility that does not tolerate any negligence". The attacks highlight the continuing security challenges in Libya, where rival administrations and armed groups have retained influence despite a ‌2020 ⁠ceasefire that halted major warfare. The country split in 2014 after a NATO-backed uprising that toppled longtime leader Muammar ⁠Gaddafi in 2011. Two governments are currently vying for power: the United Nations-recognised administration in Tripoli, led by Prime Minister Abdul Hamid Dbeibah, and a rival in the east backed by military commander Khalifa Haftar. In a statement, the Tripoli-based government said Dbeibah held a meeting earlier in the day with key officials, including the interior minister and the chiefs of some armed groups in the capital, "to follow up on the latest security developments". Dbeibah "stressed the need to deal firmly with any transgressions or actions that threaten security or harm vital facilities and installations", the statement said. Separately, a Libyan parliamentary panel condemned the attack and called for stronger protection of oil installations. "The House of Representatives' Energy and Natural Resources Committee condemns in the strongest terms the criminal attack targeting the Zawiya Refinery, one of the most vital facilities in the oil and gas sector that is a cornerstone of the national economy," it said in a statement.

headline: King Charles’ Death Report Mistakenly Airs on Radio Station After Staffer Played Announcement ‘Out of Curiosity’
body of the article: In May, the U.K. radio station Radio Caroline aired three pre-recorded statements mistakenly announcing that King Charles had died On Aug. 10, U.K. media regulator Ofcom issued a report on the incident, finding that the station breached two broadcast codes Radio Caroline said a staffer looked at the files "out of curiosity" and they interrupted a show being streamed offsite A U.K. radio station that mistakenly aired premature reports thatKing Charlesdied in May breached broadcast standards, the country's media regulator Ofcom said. On May 19, Radio Caroline aired three pre-recorded statements claiming that King Charles, 77, died duringThe Barry Marsh Show. The Office of Communications (Ofcom) said it received two complaints about the reports, which interrupted regular music programming. Credit: Tommy Forbes/Bango Studios/Getty In the third statement, the radio station said "news media" confirmed King Charles died. The national anthem was then played before one of the statements was repeated. There was then about 16 minutes of silence, according to Ofcom's report. King Charles in JuneCredit: Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty After the moments of silence, regular programming resumed. The host apologized to listeners about 30 minutes after the statements aired, confirming King Charles was not dead. "I've just been informed that we've played in error some information a little earlier, I didn't hear this myself, but it is incorrect, it's a technical issue, and of course we apologize," the host said. In itsMonday, Aug. 10, bulletin, Ofcom said it considered the situation a breach of two rules under the Broadcasting Code. "News, in whatever form, must be reported with due accuracy and presented with due impartiality," reads the first code. "Significant mistakes in news should normally be acknowledged and corrected on air quickly. Corrections should be appropriately scheduled…" reads the second code. Can't get enough of PEOPLE's Royals coverage? Sign up forour free Royals newsletterto get the latest updates on Kate Middleton, Meghan Markle and more! Radio Caroline, which mostly broadcasts music from the 1960s to today, said the host's show was streaming from a remote location at the time of the incident. Meanwhile, a staffer was performing maintenance on a studio computer and found the three files prepared for King Charles' death. Radio Caroline "explained that these files are accompanied with 'a set of strict instructions to presenters and managers' to follow before being aired, but, out of curiosity, the member of staff played the files, which stopped the stream from the presenter's remote location, and broadcast the files on air," Ofcom's bulletin reads. After the staffer realized what happened, they stopped playing the files and left the office. The show's host, who was on a call, did not notice that they had been mistakenly aired. After the host realized an incorrect program was being streamed, he contacted a station engineer who already knew what happened and was investigating. They then switched to the regular program. King Charles in AprilCredit: Samir Hussein/Samir Hussein/WireImage Radio Caroline "took the matter very seriously, and much activity was taking place during those 30 minutes leading up to the apology" and the station's staff acted "as soon as they could," the station told Ofcom. The staffer who played the incorrect files was "reprimanded" and has since "apologized," the station told Ofcom, adding that the files now exist on an external hard drive. Hosts and staff were also "reminded of the relevant procedures," the station told Ofcom. PEOPLE reached out to Radio Caroline for further comment. Read the original article onPeople

headline: 2 police officers attacked, wounded in France; suspect arrested
body of the article: Aug. 10 (UPI) -- Two police officers in southern France were attacked and wounded by a bladed weapon-wielding assailant Monday evening, officials said, in what may have been a terrorism-related attack. The suspect was apprehended, Toulouse Mayor Jean-Luc Moudenc said ina statement. The pair of municipal officers were patrolling Rue d'Austerlitz when attacked, he said, stating both were taken to Rangueil University Hospital for treatment. Officials did not comment on their conditions. He said, "remarks of a terrorist nature were also reported." "My thoughts are with our officers, their families and their colleagues," Moudenc said. "I offer them my full support and wish them a speedy recovery." Uncorroborated video of the arrest posted online shows a man fighting with three police officers, two of whom are wielding batons, on the sidewalk of an empty street. The suspect gets past two officers and lunges at a third, who sprays him with an apparent irritant. As the suspect attacks that officer, one of the others grabs him around the neck and tackles him to the ground. Alliance Police Nationale, a major French police union, said the suspect allegedly shouted "Allahu Akbar," an Arabic expression meaning "God is greatest," during the attack. "Behind the uniform, it is people who are being attacked. But what they represent is also being targeted: order, the law and authority," Alliance PN said inan online statement. "Unreserved support for our colleagues." Toulouse is the capital of France's southern Occitanie region and is located near the France-Spain border and 420 miles south of Paris. France remains onheightened terrorismalert-level since June 22. On July 27, three womenwere attackedwith a man armed with knifes in Paris. The suspect was subdued by bystanders, and an off-duty police officer detained him. The women were hospitalized, withthe last being dischargedlate last week.

headline: Colombia searches for over 3,000 missing after a powerful earthquake kills more than 100
body of the article: PEREIRA, Colombia (AP) — Search and rescue efforts resumed Tuesday in dozens of cities and towns in westernColombiaafter a powerfulearthquakeleft over 3,000 missing, with many trapped under the debris. Mayors and governors from Cali, Pereira, Choco and Manizalez said Tuesday at least 179 people had died in those four areas; the federal government, which last updated its estimates in the hours after the 7.4 magnitude earthquake hit Monday, has said at least 111 died. Around 1,600 buildings across the region have been reported damaged or collapsed. Soldiers, rescue personnel and families picked through the rubble, passing large pieces of concrete by hand along lines of volunteers. Standing near the remains of his brother's collapsed apartment building in Pereira, Jairo Vargas said he made the 220-kilometer (135-mile) drive from Medellin, hoping to find him alive. "I'm absolutely certain he's here. Absolutely certain," Vargas said, adding that his brother's car was parked outside. But he fears his sibling did not survive. "The debris surrounding my brother is soft," he said, as heavy machinery rumbled through the debris. "It's possible that it's protecting him, but we can't hear any noises anymore. I don't know. I have little hope." Choco, the region surrounding the quake's epicenter, is one of Colombia's poorest and most neglected regions, often beset by warring armed groups. Much of Choco is accessible only by boat, through the jungle or by airplane. Little was known about the extent of damage there. President Abelardo De la Espriella, who wasinaugurated just days earlier, traveled to Choco's capital, Quibdo, on Monday night and announced he was mobilizing "the entire military and police apparatus" to respond, deploying engineers, rescue workers and search dogs. "Choco will never again be the 'land of the forgotten,'" he said. The earthquake presents the first major test for de la Espriella, who is a divisive figure because of his pledge to crack down on criminal groups in the Andean nation. Families posted information aboutmissing loved oneson citizen-run websites. Dana Carolina Zamora posted an image of her missing 60-year-old uncle, Miguel Ángel Zamora, cradling his dog. The farmer was living in a rural area of El Cairo, not far from the quake's epicenter in San Jose Del Palmar. Local authorities said 80% of El Cairo, a town of about 7,000 people, was damaged. Zamora said her uncle lived in a traditional house of sticks and mud. "We are afraid. We hope that is not the case, that he is all right and that it is only a communication failure. But we haven't heard anything from him," Zamora said. The earthquake left many people unnerved afterback-to-back quakesdevastated neighboring Venezuela in late June, destroying hundreds of buildings andkilling more than 6,300 people. Mónica Sánchez owns a small company that makes work uniforms. Her home city, Pereira, was one of the worst hit, and a wall inside the factory collapsed. Sánchez and her 12 workers got outside just in time. "It was shocking — the city fell down around us," she said. Pereira's municipal government said at least 58 buildings collapsed, while Cali Mayor Alejandro Eder said at least 40 buildings had collapsed. Both cities enforced curfews Monday night to prevent looting. And in Pereira, the city government has banned privately owned vehicles from circulating, to clear the way for ambulances, police and rescue workers. The U.S. State Department has announced it would provide $15.5 million for emergency shelter, food and other aid. Governments across Latin America have also lined up to help. "This has been a tragedy for the whole city, for thousands of families," Pereira Mayor Mauricio Salazar told local media, his voice quavering. "But here we are, and we will continue forward with the hand of God." ___ Suarez reported from Bogota, Colombia, and Janetsky reported from Mexico City.

headline: Taiwan packed its new coast guard vessels with anti-ship missiles. Now it's readying them for a fight with China.
body of the article: Taiwan held a littoral combat drill on Saturday headlined by a coast guard vessel, the Bali. It's an Anping-class frigate, one of 12, that can be fitted with 16 anti-ship missiles. It's part of Taiwan's strategy for the coast guard to serve as a second navy in the event of war. TSOYING, TAIWAN — One of Taiwan's new missile-capable coast guard vessels led amajor littoral drillon Saturday, as the island entered the fourth day of its annual military exercises. The Bali, an Anping-class ship, headlined the joint drill on Taiwan's southwest coast that simulated an amphibious landing attack by Chinese forces. Four of the island's smaller Kuang-6 missile boats, special forces on rigid-hull inflatable boats, andmid-range attack dronesalso featured. Taiwan's president, Lai Ching-te, watched the Kuang-6 boats launch a rapid sortie as the Bali held position in Tsoying Port, Taiwan's largest naval base. It later sailed out to The CG606 Bali, an Anping-class frigate, is a coast guard vessel capable of firing anti-ship missiles.Matthew Loh for Business Insider In wartime, the 750-ton Anping-class frigate can be fitted with up to 16 of Taiwan's homegrown Hsiung Feng anti-ship missiles, fired from containerized box launchers mounted at an upward angle. The Bali was loaded with these box launchers in a separate drill on Thursday. Its inclusion in Saturday's drill, run primarily by the Taiwanese navy, shows how the island plans for its coast guard to operate jointly with its main fighting fleet in the event of war. The frigates' missile capability turns them essentially into dual-use ships. Taiwan can use the vessels to patrol its waters during peacetime and convert them into secondary warships within hours. The patrol vessel is heavily based on a Taiwanese naval corvette, the Tuo Chiang, and features a catamaran hull that allows it to sail more smoothly and faster in the rough seas of theTaiwan Strait. The Hsiung Feng II and III are Taiwan's homegrown anti-ship missiles, and can be fired from mobile ground launchers or vessels like the Anping-class frigate.SAM YEH/AFP via Getty Images They're fairly new: Taiwan commissioned the final of its 12 Anping-class vessels in May. Taipei has built the fleet as it grows increasingly concerned over Chinese gray-zone warfare, or hostile actions that don't constitute a declaration of war, such as intercepting Taiwanese civilian boats or repeatedly crossing into the island's territorial waters. If all of the dozen Anping-class frigates are fully equipped for war, Taiwan's coast guard could field a second navy that could be armed with up to 192 anti-ship missiles at once. Local media outletLiberty Timesreported on Monday that Taipei is stockpiling an additional 96 reserve missiles for the coast guard, bringing its total arsenal to 288. Beijing also fields anextensive coast guard fleet, which includes over 250 vessels each displacing over 500 tons, that international observers say could easily be requisitioned to support or supplement its navy. A Kuang-6 missile boat prepares for a rapid sortie.Matthew Loh for Business Insider Taiwan is running its 42nd annual Han Kuang exercise, an islandwide simulation of amainland China attack. This year's drills are expected to run for a total of 10 days and 9 nights. If you enjoyed this story, be sure to followBusiness Insideron Yahoo.

headline: Colombia rescuers search rubble after earthquake kills more than 100
body of the article: More than 100 people have died after Colombia was hit by its strongest earthquake in decades, as the government declared a state of emergency. Rescue workers were searching collapsed buildings for survivors on Monday as authorities warned that the death toll could rise further. At least 111 people have been killed in the magnitude 7.4 earthquake, President Abelardo de la Espriella said during a crisis meeting on Monday afternoon. Many people were believed to be trapped under the rubble. The quake struck at around 7:34 am (1234 GMT), with its epicentre near the town of San José del Palmar in western Colombia, the Colombian Geological Service (SGC) said. It struck at a depth of around 103 kilometres and was followed by numerous aftershocks. "The first priority is rescuing people buried under the rubble," de la Espriella said, adding that the government was mobilizing all available resources. At a later press conference in Cali, south of the epicentre, de la Espriella said 188 people were missing in the city, while 35 had been killed and around 700 injured. He said three hospitals and about 40 buildings had collapsed entirely. Another 400 soldiers were due to join the 600 already deployed to help with search and rescue operations, the president said. Cali's airport was also operating on a limited basis because of damage. More than 1,500 homes were severely damaged in several cities, including Pereira, Cali and Manizales. Sixty people were killed in Pereira alone, according to the latest figures from the city authorities. Eleven more were missing, the city said in a post on X. The full extent of the disaster remained unclear. In Cali, residents joined rescue workers searching the rubble for survivors. "We have a four-storey building here that has completely collapsed. We have already managed to rescue three people alive," a fire service official in the La Alameda neighbourhood told broadcaster Caracol. Power supplies, telephone services and other communication links have been disrupted. Six airports were closed to commercial traffic because of damage to infrastructure, de la Espriella said. The cathedral in Manizales was also severely damaged. Cars swayed in the streets, windows rattled and people fled their homes in panic. "At first I thought it was something minor. But when it kept getting stronger and didn't stop, I thought we were going to die," a woman from Manizales told broadcaster La FM. "Part of the roof of my house collapsed and the walls are cracked," Juan Bernal from the city of Armenia said. The earthquake was also felt in Bogotá, Medellín, Popayán and Armenia, as well as the neighbouring countries of Venezuela, Ecuador and Panama. The quake comes after twin earthquakes hit neighbouring Venezuela in late June, killing more than 6,000 people. However, the Colombian Geological Service said there was no connection between the earthquakes. The Venezuelan quakes involved movement of the Caribbean Plate, while the Colombian earthquake was linked to the Nazca Plate off the country's Pacific coast. The strongest previous earthquake occurred off the coast between Ecuador and Colombia in 1958 and had a magnitude of 7.6. Fifteen people were killed, according to the Geological Service. In 1999, more than 1,000 people were killed when a magnitude 6.1 earthquake struck Armenia and surrounding communities. Rescue workers arrive at the scene after a 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck Colombia. headline: 'Thankful to be alive': Video captures harrowing escape during Bradley Creek wildfire
body of the article: Many people are paying attention to a terrifying evacuation scene near Vernon, British Columbia, Canada, after a wildfire evacuee described fleeing the area. With the Bradley Creek wildfire burning nearby,CBC News reportedthat Avery Brownell was "one of the last people allowed through Westside Road." Footage shared byCBC News on TikTokshows Brownell capturing their evacuation during their escape from the Bradley Creek wildfire. In the post's caption, CBC News stated Brownell was "thankful to be alive and safe" and that they said on social media that this was "the scariest moment of their lives." Wildfires are immediate threats to all life, public health, the environment, and local economies. When flames move close to homes and evacuation routes, families can lose access to their livelihoods and ability to survive within hours. Worsening extreme weather events endanger people by putting communities in physical danger and creating long-term instability. Wildfire smoke can also worsen asthma and other health conditions. And damage to infrastructure can leave entire regions facing steep recovery costs. For people in wildfire-prone regions, emergency planning can make a major difference. That includes keeping evacuation routes in mind, preparing a go-bag with medications and important documents, and signing up for local emergency alerts in advance. Households can also reduce risk around the home by clearing dry brush and cleaning gutters. Those steps will not stop a large wildfire, but they can improve safety and buy valuable time. At the community level, stronger emergency preparation, fire response coordination, and infrastructure planning all matter when fires intensify near populated areas. TikTok users flooded the comments. One user said, "How terrifying. I'm glad you were able to make it out. incredibly devastating for the wildlife and people." headline: Rescuers race for survivors after Colombia quake kills 111
body of the article: Rescue workers continued to dig through the wreckage in a frantic search for survivors following a catastrophic earthquake on Aug. 10 inwestern Colombia, the South American nation's worst this century. The 7.4 magnitude temblor killed at least 111 people just days after the country's new president was sworn in and came nearly seven weeks aftertwin quakesdevastated neighboring Venezuela, killing more than 6,000. President AbelardoDe La Espriella, who officially took office Aug. 7, said the immediate priority remains freeing those trapped beneath the rubble. "The national government has all of its capabilities deployed to protect lives, assist affected communities and deliver aid wherever it is needed," he said in a national address declaring a national emergency. The quake struck at 7:34 a.m. local time, damaging hospitals, infrastructure and residential towers, causing widespread communications outages and prompting authorities to suspend operations at multiple airports. In the absence of heavy equipment, rescue workers, police and volunteers shoveled debris by hand at many sites, looking for survivors. Risaralda, in the central Andean region known for its coffee, seemed to suffer the brunt of the damage. In the capital city of Pereira, where the collapse of a four-story building was captured on video, rescue workers dug through the crumbled remains of structures seeking signs of life. In Manizales, also within the country's coffee growing axis, other footage showed a tower atop the city's landmark Gothic cathedral toppled from its foundation. In Cali, the capital of Valle del Cauca, Juan Carlos Osorio told Caracol Television that neighbors at one felled structure site had formed human chains to speed up debris removal with "many people trapped" beneath the rubble. The collapse of the building, he said, "sounded like a bomb." Colombia is located along the seismically active Pacific Ring of Fire, recording thousands of mostly minor quakes monthly. In 1999, cities in the country's coffee region, including Armenia and Pereira, were hit by a massive 6.2 magnitude quake that killed more than 1,000 people. Colombia's Pacific region, especially the portion hit by Monday's quake, is among the nation's poorest and partially nestled in dense jungle,The Guardianreported. The quake was felt in nearby Ecuador and Panama, the newspaper said. Suzan van der Lee, a seismologist at Northwestern University in Evanston, Illinois, said the quake's magnitude, inland location and strike-slip motion may have aggravated damage in populated valleys despite its notable depth. "This one was far below the crust, and in theory it shouldn't cause as much shaking," van der Lee said. The nation's civil aviation authority suspended operations at several airports in the country's west, including Pereira, Manizales, Quibdo, Armenia, Cartago and Buenaventura, pending structural inspections. The situation poses a significant test for De La Espriella, a former lawyer who has never held political office. The rightwing candidate,endorsed byU.S. PresidentDonald Trump, bested leftist senator Ivan Cepedain a June runoffafter vowing tough crackdowns on crime and proposing to build mega-prisons. Contributing: Reuters This article originally appeared on USA TODAY:Rescuers race for survivors after Colombia quake kills 111

headline: Body of Girl, 11, Discovered in River in Scotland After ‘Unexplained’ Death
body of the article: The body of 11-year-old Faith Curran was reported missing in Midlothian, Scotland, on Aug. 6 Her body was discovered hours later in the Gore Glen River near Shanks Bridge Authorities are treating her death as "unexplained" but do not believe there are suspicious circumstances The body of an 11-year-old girl was found in a river in Scotland hours after her family reported she was missing. Faith Curran's family reported that the young girl was missing on Aug. 6 around 12:40 p.m. in the Gore Glen area of Midlothian, Police Scotland Midlothian said in astatement. Curran's body was discovered in the river near Shanks Bridge around 4:25 p.m., and her family was alerted. Her death is being treated as "unexplained," but authorities say they do not believe there are any "suspicious circumstances." Scotland's public prosecutor, the Procurator Fiscal, will conduct a review into her death, police said. Curran was remembered by her family as a "happy, adventurous, and outgoing girl who enjoyed life." A memorial was created at Gore Glen Woodland Park, with a teddy bear and flowers placed together on the bridge, theBBCreports. The Gore Glen is Scotland's first industrial-scale gunpowder mill and was established in 1794. Midlothian is approximately 11 miles south of Edinburgh. Read the original article onPeople

headline: King Charles, 77, Reflects on His Near-Death Experience
body of the article: King Charles III offered a rare reflection on the avalanche that almost killed him and claimed the life of one of his close friends nearly 40 years ago. The 77-year-old monarch reportedly spoke about the 1988 incident while hosting members of the Assynt Mountain Rescue Team at the Castle of Mey in Scotland on August 1. The gathering marked the 50th anniversary of the mountain rescue group. During the conversation, Charles, who was then the Prince of Wales, reportedly described his survival in the avalanche as "a close thing." "He spoke of the near miss he had in that avalanche in the context of the dangers mountains contain," Ben Dyson, the team's leader,told The Times. "Obviously after all these years it is still much in his memory, but it had given him an insight into the valuable work we do and the dangers we face," Dyson said. The avalanche struck on March 10, 1988, while Charles and a group of friends were skiing off-piste above Klosters, Switzerland, a resort long favored by the royal family. A wall of snow swept down the mountain, killing Major Hugh Lindsay, a former equerry toQueen Elizabeth IIand a close friend of Charles. Another member of the group, Patti Palmer-Tomkinson, suffered serious leg injuries. Charles and other members of the party managed to escape the avalanche. They later returned with their guide and a Swiss police officer to help dig Lindsay and Palmer-Tomkinson out of the snow. Lindsay was pronounced dead at a hospital in nearby Davos. He was 34. Lindsay's wife, Sarah, was six months pregnant when he died. Their daughter, Alice, was born later that year, with Charles becoming her godfather. The tragedy has rarely been discussed publicly by the king in the decades since. He later wrote in a letter, "I still find it hard to understand why I survived and he didn't,"The Guardian reported. Princess Diana and Sarah Ferguson were also on the ski trip but were at their chalet when the avalanche struck. Diana later said she had been sick with the flu and had stayed behind that day, narrowly avoiding the disaster. Charles, who had been skiing since the 1960s, has since stepped away from the sport. During a 2025 visit to England, he told a Swiss man, "I think my skiing days are behind me,"according toHello! Magazine.

headline: Australia adds optional gender identity and sexual orientation questions to census
body of the article: MELBOURNE, Australia (AP) — Australians for the first time can reveal theirsexual orientationand whether they identify as a differentgenderthan the one recorded at birth — contentious debut questions in the latestcensusthat occurs every five years. The 66-question census, held on Tuesday, Aug. 11, is the first under a center-leftLabor Partygovernment since 2011. The current Labor government backflipped to allow the questions after having dropped them temporarily two years ago as "divisive." Both questions are open to members of households 16 years of age and older. The answer options for sexual orientation are straight, gay or lesbian, bisexual, don't know, prefer not to answer or a term of the respondent's choice that can be written in a designated blank space. The options for the gender that the respondent currently identifies with that differs from that registered at birth are man, woman, nonbinary, prefer not to answer or another term that the respondent can provide. The gender and sexual orientation questions are optional, along with a question on religion that has been included since the first census in 1911. Labor had promised such questions about sexuality and gender would be included in the next census while campaigning ahead of the 2022 elections that brought the party to power after nine years out of government. The Australian government determines the topics for each census. The Australian Bureau of Statistics decides the wording of questions. In 2024, the government decided against deviating from the 2021 census questions in the interests of maintaining social cohesion. "We do not want to open up divisive debates in the community now," Deputy Prime MinisterRichard Marlessaid in August 2024. The government soon relented after almost a week of backlash from LGBTQ+ advocates and criticism from some Labor lawmakers. Two days after Marles spoke, Prime MinisterAnthony Albanese, a heterosexual who has marched in the annual Sydney Gay and Lesbian Mardi Gras twice since he took office in 2022, confirmed in a radio interview that a question about sexual orientation would be included in the next census. ABS Chief Statistician David Gruen said his bureau discovered a "substantial level of interest in asking questions on gender and sexual orientation" during public consultations ahead of the census. "For a proportion of the population … collecting this information is very important. But for other people, it's information that they simply don't want to share," Gruen told Australian Broadcasting Corp, referencing the decision to make the questions optional. Liz Allen, an Australian National University demographer, said Australia lagged behind some like-minded countries in dealing with gender and sexual orientation in the census.Britainasked similar questions of its population in 2021, New Zealand in 2023 and Canada three months ago. "We've been talking about these questions for some time, but theprevious government, it didn't look like they were going to budge on the evidence and enable it to be in the census. So the ABS (Australian Bureau of Statistics) really didn't put it to them," Allen said. Allen said the questions need to go further into the issues of sexuality and gender by asking respondents if they wereintersex— a term for people born with biological sex characteristics such as chromosomes, hormones, or genitals that do not fit typical definitions of male or female. The lastU.S. censusin 2020 allowed only two responses to its gender question: male or female. That census, which is held once a decade, did not specifically ask about sexual orientation. But same-sex relationships were for the first time allowed to be listed in the household relationship field. In Australia, people were asked to submit their census answer forms as soon as they received their instructions in the mail if they knew where they would be on census night. The ABS expects 85% of responses will be madeonline, up from almost 80% in 2021, when almost half the population was in pandemic lockdown. The ABS also provides paper census forms on request. Field staff help homeless people and people living in remote areas participate. Failing to comply with a direction to complete the census can result in a fine of up to 364 Australian dollars ($257) a day. The ABS said more than 5 million forms had been submitted by Tuesday morning. Almost 11 million forms are expected to be completed.

headline: Fast-moving wildfire sends more than 20,000 fleeing in British Columbia, Canada
body of the article: Communities along Okanagan Lake in the Canadian province of British Columbia emptied out as more than 20,000 residents were ordered to leave while crews battled a rapidly spreading wildfire. Authorities said aircraft were deployed to pull dozens of residents to safety while prolonged drought, high temperatures, and wind drove dangerous fire activity. At least one person may have been killed amid the disaster, according to reports. After the Bald Range wildfire — firstreportedon August 7 — ripped through areas near Summerland and Peachland, British Columbia declared a state of emergency. According to CBS News, the province had more than 100 active wildfires as of August 8, with nearly half considered out of control. Officials ordered evacuations in Summerland, home to about 12,000 people, and for roughly 8,000 more people in and around Peachland. Premier David Eby's office said there had been "significant structure loss," but authorities could not fully assess the damage because the fire zone remained too active. By August 9, CBS reported, the blaze grew to more than 53 square miles and pushed roughly 9 miles toward Okanagan Lake. Eby called it "a remarkable escalation in fire activity" and said the wildfire had become so intense it created its own weather system, including lightning. Resident Anette Boulet, speaking from an evacuation center in Penticton, told CBS the advancing fire "looked like doomsday." Road closures added to the impacts. Highway 97, a key corridor through the region, was shut between Peachland and Penticton as evacuees packed the roads, making both departures and emergency response harder. The Royal Canadian Mounted Police are investigating a possible wildfire death near Summerland, although dangerous conditions have made confirmation difficult. British Columbia averages about 1,600 wildfires annually, and fire seasons across Canada have grown more severe, sending smoke over broad areas of Canada and the United States. By declaring an emergency across the province, British Columbia gained broader powers to manage the crisis, including restricting travel and securing accommodations for evacuees. Forests Minister Ravi Parmar said 18 firefighting aircraft were used to rescue more than 50 people. Search-and-rescue crews were continuing to look for others who might have been trapped as the fire advanced. According to Cliff Chapman, director of operations for the British Columbia Wildfire Service, conditions were "explosive." headline: Harry Potter Fans Saved Dobby’s “Grave” From A $580 Million Power Cable, But The New Route Has Its Own Twist
body of the article: Harry Potter fans helped push a major power cable away from Dobby's "grave" in Wales, only for the changed route to pass close to real ancient burial remains. The dispute involved theGreenlink Interconnector, a high-voltage electricity link between Ireland and Great Britain. The Guardian reported that the £430 million project, roughly $580 million, was rerouted after fans complained that the original path would disturb the Freshwater West memorial associated with Dobby fromHarry Potter and the Deathly Hallows. The fan tribute sits at Freshwater West in Pembrokeshire, where Dobby's beach burial was filmed for the final Harry Potter movies. Visitors have long left stones, socks and other items at the site, even after conservation warnings about the protected coastal area. Greenlink project manager Simon Ludlam said the team found a way around the fictional house elf's memorial. The route that followed still brought planners close to Bronze Age remains, including urns associated with human burial. Ludlam discussed the route controversy on theEnergy Revolutionpodcast, according toThe Guardian. He said the Greenlink route was originally set to pass through the area associated with Dobby's memorial at Freshwater West. The reaction began after Ludlam pointed out the planned cable route during a BBC interview. Once viewers realized where the underground cable could go, Greenlink received hundreds of calls from Harry Potter fans concerned about the tribute. Ludlam said he initially did not know who Dobby was. A colleague eventually explained that the company was being accused of planning to run the cable through Dobby's "grave," turning a film-location memorial into a real planning headache. The company then worked with planners to move the route away from the fan site. Ludlam said people were pleased once the memorial was avoided, joking that "Dobby's happy." The changed path came with its own awkward detail. Ludlam said the route went close to real Bronze Age remains instead, while still avoiding the fictional grave. The Guardian reported that the remains included urns associated with human burial. The cable has since gone into operation. Ireland's Department of Climate, Energy and the Environment said in April 2025 that the 500MW Greenlink Interconnector had entered commercial operations after construction and testing. The memorial grew from the Harry Potter films rather than the books alone. Freshwater West was used for the beach burial scene inHarry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, and fans later began leaving painted stones, socks and messages at the real location. The socks come from Dobby's story in the series, where receiving clothing represents freedom for a house elf. Over time, that connection turned the beach into a pop culture pilgrimage site for visitors who wanted to mark the character's death. The same popularity has caused problems at Freshwater West. The beach is managed by National Trust Cymru and sits in an environmentally sensitive coastal area. In 2022, National Trust Cymru allowed the Dobby memorial to remain at Freshwater West in the immediate term after a consultation. It also asked visitors to stop leaving objects at the site. ITV Newsreported at the time that the Trust warned against leaving socks, trinkets and painted pebbles because they could enter the marine environment and food chain. That earlier warning made the cable dispute more complicated than a simple fan victory. The memorial was protected from the cable route, but conservation groups had already said the beach needed fewer objects left behind. Greenlink connects EirGrid's Great Island substation in County Wexford with National Grid's Pembroke substation in Pembrokeshire. The project uses subsea and underground cables to link the Irish and British electricity grids. The company has described Greenlink as a 500MW interconnector designed to support energy security, regional investment and the integration of low-carbon energy. Its Welsh route comes ashore at Freshwater West before continuing underground toward the Pembroke area. Greenlink previously said the Pembrokeshire section included a subsea cable coming ashore under the beach and dunes at Freshwater West, then continuing underground to a converter station near the existing National Grid substation.

headline: Russia launches ballistic missile strikes on Ukraine, killing five
body of the article: Russia launched fresh ballistic missile attacks on Kiev and other major Ukrainian cities, Ukrainian officials said, killing at least five people and injuring 20 in the southern city of Zaporizhzhya. Regional military administrator Ivan Fedorov said on Telegram early on Tuesday that industrial facilities and infrastructure had been hit in Zaporizhzhya. One person was initially reported injured in Kiev. Mayor Vitali Klitschko said explosions had been heard in the capital and urged residents to remain in shelters while emergency crews were deployed. The Kyiv Independent reported that Russia had launched another ballistic missile attack. Ukraine's air force also warned that Russian missiles were heading towards the cities of Sumy, Kharkiv and Chernihiv, according to the report. Ukraine has struggled with shortages of air defence interceptor missiles after more than four years of war, allowing Russia to intensify its use of ballistic missiles against Kiev and other cities. US-made Patriot systems are considered among the most effective defences against ballistic missiles, which are particularly difficult to intercept because of their high speed. Ukraine has several Patriot systems but lacks sufficient interceptor missiles. Officials in Kiev fear that Russia could again severely damage the country's infrastructure with missile attacks over the coming winter, worsening conditions for millions of Ukrainians.

headline: Radio Staffer Played King Charles Death Announcement ‘Out of Curiosity’ Then Panicked and Ran Away
body of the article: A British radio station's bizarre false announcement that King Charles III had died has taken an even stranger turn, with regulators revealing that the mistake began when a staff member deliberately played prerecorded royal-death files "out of curiosity." Radio Caroline shocked listeners on May 19 when its normal programming was interrupted by solemn announcements saying the King had died. "God Save the King" followed before the station fell silent for around 16 minutes. At the time, station manager Peter Moore blamed a "computer error" that had accidentally activated Radio Caroline's "Death of a Monarch" procedure. A new Ofcom ruling found that a staff member carrying out maintenance on the studio computer had accessed the prerecorded files and played them without realizing the audio would go out live. After discovering what had happened, the staffer stopped the files, "panicked and left the premises." Ofcom ultimately ruled that Radio Caroline breached two sections of the Broadcasting Code over the false announcement and the time it took to properly correct it. The incident happened duringThe Barry Marsh Showwhile another staff member was performing maintenance on Radio Caroline's studio computer. According to Ofcom's findings, the staff member discovered sound files that had been prerecorded for use following the death of the monarch. Radio Caroline told the regulator that the files were accompanied by "a set of strict instructions to presenters and managers" explaining what needed to happen before they could be used. The person responsible was not Barry Marsh, who was presenting the show remotely.The Independentinitially identified the presenter as the person who left before correcting its report to make clear that it was another staff member. The prerecorded material was intended for one of the most consequential events a British broadcaster could be required to cover. One announcement told listeners that Radio Caroline had suspended its normal programming "as a mark of respect following the passing of His Majesty King Charles III." Another said the King had died and that the station would play continuous suitable music until further notice. When Marsh returned to the air, he told listeners he had just been informed that incorrect information had been played earlier. "I didn't hear this myself, but it is incorrect, it's a technical issue, and of course we apologise," he said. Ofcom received two complaints about the broadcast. Rule 5.1 requires news, in whatever form, to be reported with due accuracy and presented with due impartiality. Rule 5.2 requires significant mistakes in news to be acknowledged and corrected on air quickly. Ofcom described the false report of the King's death as a "very significant inaccuracy about an issue of particular public importance." The regulator said Radio Caroline did not broadcast an adequate apology and clarification until approximately 30 minutes after the inaccurate announcements first went out. Ofcom acknowledged that the station was monitoring its output and that an engineer knew there was a problem. However, it took time to determine what had happened and restore the scheduled programming. The response was further complicated because Marsh was presenting the program remotely. The Ofcom findings provide considerably more detail than Radio Caroline disclosed immediately after the incident. On May 20, station manager Peter Moore issued a public statement attributing the false announcement to a technical problem. "Due to a computer error at our main studio, the Death of a Monarch procedure, which all UK stations hold in readiness while hoping not to require, was accidentally activated on Tuesday afternoon (19 May), mistakenly announcing that HM the King had passed away," Moore wrote. "Radio Caroline then fell silent as would be required, which alerted us to restore programming and issue an on-air apology." "We apologise to HM the King and to our listeners for any distress caused," he added.The Guardianand other outlets reported that explanation at the time. While Radio Caroline was mistakenly announcing his death, Charles was carrying out public engagements in Northern Ireland with Queen Camilla. The Royal Family's official record confirms that the couple arrived in Belfast on May 19 for a three-day visit. At Thompson Dock in the Titanic Quarter, Charles and Camilla met performers, organizers and volunteers preparing for Fleadh Cheoil na hÉireann and watched a showcase of music and cultural performances. They also visited Titanic Distillers in the restored Edwardian pumphouse, where they learned about the whiskey-making process and sampled whiskey. Later that day, Charles visited W5 LIFE, an initiative focused on digital skills, while the King and Queen ended the day by receiving Northern Ireland's first minister and deputy first minister at Hillsborough Castle. Charles continued with engagements in Northern Ireland the following day. Radio Caroline told Ofcom that it took the incident seriously and acted to prevent the same mistake from happening again. The staff member responsible for playing the recordings was reprimanded and apologized, according to the station. Radio Caroline also removed the royal-death files from the desktop of the studio computer so they could not be accessed in the same way. Presenters and support staff were reminded of the procedures governing the material and the steps required before any such announcement could be broadcast.

headline: Off Alaska, reports question whether both of Zuckerberg's superyachts ignored distress calls
body of the article: A superyacht and a support vessel owned by Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg reportedly traveled past a stranded boat off Alaska without stopping. However, one key detail remains unconfirmed: There is no public proof that either yacht was directly asked to assist and then refused. According toLuxurylaunches, the controversy centers on Launchpad, Zuckerberg's luxury superyacht, and Wingman, its support vessel, following an overnight boating incident that left a boat stranded. Neither boat responded to the smaller boat's requests for assistance, and cruise ship Wilderness Legacy instead provided help. Michael Love, who was aboard Wilderness Legacy, said the ship's captain told passengers that Launchpad had been closer to the smaller boat and had not responded. He later said he had only heard that portion from others and did not witness it himself. Love said the incident took place at about 1 a.m. and that Wilderness Legacy ultimately moved toward the stranded vessel. He said the rescue unfolded close enough for him to observe it from his cabin. The article later described a review of historical AIS, or Automatic Identification System, data that appeared to place Launchpad ahead of Wilderness Legacy in the same area, with the yacht slowing or stopping before continuing on. Wilderness Legacy, meanwhile, appears to have turned toward the smaller boat. However, AIS data cannot reveal what happened on the yacht's bridge, cannot confirm whether the crew received any Coast Guard transmission, and cannot show whether Zuckerberg was even on board at the time. The YouTube channelThe Yacht Report(@YachtReport)examinedan eyewitness account, vessel-tracking data, and the rules governing assistance at sea. Helping at sea is not simply a courtesy. In remote Alaskan waters, where darkness, weather, and distance can quickly turn a mechanical problem into a dangerous situation, mariners often rely on one another. International maritime law generally requires captains to help people facing genuine distress, as long as doing so would not put their own vessel, crew, or passengers in serious danger. Still, that obligation is more nuanced than it may appear online. A Coast Guard Marine Assistance Request Broadcast is not the same as a Mayday call or a confirmed distress situation. If the smaller boat needed non-emergency assistance, nearby vessels may not have faced the same legal duty they would in a true distress event. If either vessel received a direct Coast Guard instruction during a genuine emergency, the legal picture could look very different. AIS records can help reconstruct vessel movements. Distress classifications, radio protocols, and emergency broadcasts are intended to clarify when a situation is urgent and which vessels may be expected to respond. Preparation remains critical in remote coastal areas. Small-boat operators can reduce risk by carrying a working VHF radio, emergency locator equipment, and updated navigation tools. Cruise and charter passengers can also ask operators about emergency response procedures before departure. The available evidence does not settle the matter. Launchpad appears to have been in the area, and Wilderness Legacy did provide assistance, but there is still no confirmation that either of Zuckerberg's vessels turned down an actual request to help the stranded boat. headline: Colombian Influencer Kidnapped by Armed Men in La Guajira; $100 Million Peso Reward Offered
body of the article: A famous content creator and entrepreneur was kidnapped from her residence located in the countryside of a Colombian border city early Monday morning. Local authorities have announced a bounty of up to 100 million pesos for any information that would help locate her. Angie Paola Argáez Núñez, 29, was abducted around 2:30 a.m. from a private property in Campana, Los Palitos district of Maicao, La Guajira, as reported by regional media outlet Guajira News. According to reports, three or four armed men came and forcibly took Argáez Núñez with them, as stated by Guajira News. The criminals fled in a white 2018 Toyota Fortuner belonging to Argáez Núñez, according to Guajira News. Mayor of Maicao Miguel Felipe Aragón offered the bounty following a security council meeting on Monday, as stated by newspaper El Universal of Cartagena. The Mayor's Office said the bounty would be paid to anyone who would provide information regarding the whereabouts of Argáez Núñez. Police in La Guajira began implementing a lockdown across roads, villages, and border areas, according to news site Diario La Guajira. Police and army anti-kidnapping units (Gaula) are performing intelligence and patrol activities in the countryside and areas near informal border crossings. Sipol and Sijín, national police intelligence and criminal investigation departments, were involved in the search. Security cameras are also being analyzed to trace the vehicle and identify those responsible. Mayor's Office appealed to residents to provide any information that could help locate Argáez Núñez. Tips can be submitted through the 165 emergency line or via phone 321 394 0581, promising anonymity of the caller. As of Monday evening, her location remains unknown. Authorities have not mentioned any motive for the kidnapping, and it is not clear whether kidnappers have contacted her relatives. Argáez Núñez is a famous local influencer and entrepreneur. Her relatives, fans, and community groups organized an online campaign calling for her release. Maicao is located 12 miles away from the Venezuelan border and serves as a major commercial crossing point, known for its long history of smuggling and activity of armed groups. Kidnapping cases are increasing in Colombia over recent years. According to Fundación Ideas para la Paz, a Bogota-based think tank, there were 256 kidnappings in January-July 2025, which is a 57.1% increase compared to the same period in 2024. Colombia's Ministry of Defense reported 56 kidnappings in January-February 2026, compared to 50 in the same period last year. The case is under investigation. headline: Zelensky says Ukraine will step up strikes deep inside Russia
body of the article: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine would carry out further strikes against targets deep inside Russia, after Kiev confirmed an attack on Russia's oil industry in the Siberian city of Tobolsk. Zelensky said in his evening video address on Monday that Ukraine would continue attacking targets deep inside Russia to show Moscow that peace was necessary. He also again warned about North Korea's military support for Russia. Moscow had received additional ballistic missiles from Pyongyang and was preparing for another contingent of North Korean soldiers to arrive in Russia, Zelensky said, without providing evidence. North Korean weapons had been further developed in cooperation with Russia, posing a threat to countries in Asia, Zelensky said. Over the weekend, Zelensky said Russia could receive far more North Korean troops to support its war in Ukraine than previously thought, putting the number at up to 50,000 soldiers. Russia has been waging a devastating war against Ukraine for more than four years. North Korean troops were deployed in Russia in 2024 and 2025 to help Russian forces push Ukrainian troops out of the western Russian region of Kursk. Ukraine has significantly stepped up its counterattacks against Russia in recent months, relying heavily on drones.

headline: Iran installs new war chiefs as Tehran signals ‘prolonged confrontation,’ expert warns
body of the article: Iranian Supreme LeaderMojtaba Khameneiformally appointed six senior military commanders Monday, cementing a wartime reshuffle as Tehran rebuilds a command structure impacted by months of U.S. and Israeli strikes. The appointments, announced by Khamenei's office and promoted on social media, fill posts across Iran's armed forces, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and the Basij paramilitary force, with a counterterrorism expert warning the timing and language of the decrees signal Tehran is preparing for "prolonged confrontation" and not a settlement with Washington. "Strategically, the announcements made were issued in English, on X, while Iranian and Omani negotiators finalize the coordinates of a proposedshipping route through Hormuz, which is deliberate sequencing," Dr.Omar Mohammed, director of the Antisemitism Research Initiative at George Washington University's Program on Extremism, told Fox News Digital. "Tehran is establishing its command structure as a fact on the ground before it signs anything." Trump Says Iran Will Pay — What It Takes To End The War Remains Unclear Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. Mohammed also pointed to language in the appointment announcements blaming the deaths of predecessors on what Iran called the "Zionist-American enemy." Read On The Fox News App "That phrase, in formal state documents, codifies the United States as a co-belligerent," Mohammed said. Khamenei appointed Ali Abdollahi as chief of staff of the armed forces and Kioumars Heydari as his deputy. He also formally named Ahmad Vahidi commander-in-chief of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, promoting him to the rank of major general. Mostafa Izadi was named deputy IRGC commander, Ali Azmaei as commander of the IRGC Navy and Hossein Taeb as commander of the Basij. Mohammed said Vahidi was also instructed to maintain readiness for "powerful offensive operations against the enemy," by the Supreme Leader, while Abdollahi was tasked with completing the integration of the General Staff into the Khatam al-Anbiya wartime joint command. "States exiting a conflict dismantle their wartime command arrangements, but Iran is now institutionalizing its own," Mohammed said. "The decrees here describe a leadership planning for a prolonged confrontation, not a settlement." Former Iranian Interior Minister Ahmad Vahidi attends an event. Several of the newly appointed commanders have previously faced U.S. or Europeansanctionsor allegations tied to terrorism and violent crackdowns. Vahidi is the subject of anInterpol Red Noticerequested by Argentina over his alleged involvement in the 1994 bombing of the AMIA Jewish community center in Buenos Aires, which killed 85 people. Taeb, a former chief of the IRGC Intelligence Organization and former Basij commander, is on theU.S. Treasury Department's sanctions list. The United States first designated him in 2010 over serious human rights abuses following Iran's disputed 2009 presidential election. Heydari was alsosanctioned by the United States in 2022after the Treasury Department said he had publicly acknowledged his forces' involvement in the violent response to Iran's November 2019 protests, in which hundreds of protesters were killed. The European Union has also sanctioned him. Iran's Unseen Supreme Leader Becomes Weapon In Escalating Power Struggle, Experts Say The reshuffle comes as Iran continues rebuilding its political and military leadership after a series of U.S. and Israeli strikes killed senior figures across the regime. AyatollahAli Khamenei, who had served as supreme leader since 1989, was killed in a Feb. 28 strike at the start of the war. Mojtaba Khamenei, was selected as Iran's new supreme leader in March. Ali Larijani, then secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council and a major figure in the country's security and foreign policy establishment, and Gholamreza Soleimani, commander of the Basij, were killed in strikes on March 17. The latest appointments come amid continuing questions about Mojtaba Khamenei's health and public absence. President Masoud Pezeshkian claimed Monday that he had held a nearly seven-hour meeting with Khamenei, only the second meeting the president has publicly disclosed since the new supreme leader took office,Iran Internationalreported. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Gholam-Hossein Mohseni-Eje'i, the head of the judiciary and Alireza Arafi, (right) deputy chairman of the Assembly of Experts, attend the meeting of the interim leadership council of Iran in an unknown location, amid the U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran, in Iran, March 1, 2026. Khamenei has not appeared publicly since being selected in March and is believed to have been wounded in the Feb. 28 strike that killed his father. Pezeshkian said the two discussed economic conditions, sanctions and other domestic challenges and that Khamenei emphasized the need for "unity and cohesion." The military rebuild, however, has not extended fully into Iran's sensitiveintelligence apparatus, according to Mohammed. "The IRGC Intelligence Organization and its counterintelligence arm have no announced chiefs, and Iran has no permanent defense or intelligence ministers," the expert said. "The appointments require assigning responsibility for the counterintelligence failures that enabled the February decapitation. headline: Colombian Influencer Sofia Murillo Killed in Rio Sightseeing Helicopter Crash With Mother and Grandmother
body of the article: Sofia Murillo, her mother, and her grandmother died when the helicopter they had boarded to enjoy a bird's-eye view of the Christ the Redeemer statue crashed into thick forests in Rio de Janeiro, Brazilian officials and the family informed. Sofia Murillo died along with her mother, Wendy Manrique, 37, and her grandmother, Rocio Cubillos, 59, after the helicopter crash on August 8 close to the Vista Chinesa viewpoint in the Tijuca National Park. The pilot, Alessandro Rocha, also died in the crash. None of them survived the accident. Robinson R44 helicopter crashed around 11:11 a.m. in thick vegetation in the large urban forest surrounding the city, The Rio Times reported. About 40 firefighters and 11 vehicles were deployed to the scene, which was hard to access. The helicopter caught fire immediately upon impact, perTMZ. The family, hailing from Bogotá, had arranged a 20-minute panoramic flight over the city, Dexerto mentioned. The helicopter could accommodate only three passengers; hence, six family members traveling together were divided into two batches. Sofia, her mother, and her grandmother took off first. Sofia's uncle, Victor Manrique, who was waiting at the hangar with his wife and their 15-year-old daughter for the second flight, told local media outlets that the family learned about the tragic incident through news reports, according toTMZ. "We were a very happy family," Manrique told Need To Know. He described his niece as a hard-working and diligent girl and added that the family had booked the flight with the last of their vacation savings and a credit card. The relatives had gone to Brazil to celebrate a quinceañera, the traditional birthday party of 15 years of age, The Rio Times explained. The reason behind the crash remains unknown. Rio de Janeiro's Civil Police and Cenipa (the Brazilian Aeronautical Accidents Investigation and Prevention Center) are running parallel investigations, Hola reported. Cenipa, a Brazilian Air Force unit, is carrying out the technical investigation of the wreckage to find out the causes of the crash. A preliminary report is expected to be released in several weeks, and the final one will take months, The Rio Times reported. Fire damage may hinder the use of any data recorded during the flight. A lawyer for the operator, Voos Rio Panoramico, told reporters that the company has not identified the cause but stressed that the pilot was licensed, the permits were in order, and the aircraft's maintenance was up to date, Hola reported. The Brazilian National Civil Aviation Agency (ANAC) confirmed that the helicopter's certificate was valid, Diário do Rio de Janeiro reported. Panoramic flights are considered specialized air services, and for such flights, there is a special technical certification of the aircraft and the crew. ANAC stated that it is discussing with the city of Rio de Janeiro joint control of panoramic flights. Mayor Eduardo Cavaliere formally requested urgent inspection measures for the sector, including the possible temporary ban of aerial tours while the review of the situation in the city is being conducted. Murillo had amassed an audience of more than 250,000 followers on TikTok and Instagram, where she shared makeup tutorials, hair and skin care tips, and cosmetic reviews, Dexerto reported. Her last post, dated August 5th, was about a gym workout. Her fans started posting condolences on her social media pages. The crash happened almost two months after singer Oliver Tree and YouTuber Gaspi died in another helicopter accident in Rio de Janeiro, Dexerto reported.
